best_for: Windows developers and admins who need to compare two or three versions of files or folders and merge the changes, without paying for a diff tool.
description:
WinMerge is a file comparison and merging tool for Windows, maintained by volunteers as an open source project and translated into many languages. You can run it on its own or plug it into another program, such as a version control client, as the external tool for showing and merging differences.

Each comparison opens in its own tab. The editor has syntax highlighting, line numbers and word wrap, and a location pane gives you a map of where the changes sit in the file. WinMerge can spot lines that were moved rather than changed, and it reads Windows, Unix and Mac line endings. For big folder trees, a quick mode compares files by size and date, and the results can be shown as a tree.

points.title: Files, folders and three-way
points.text: WinMerge compares two or three files line by line and highlights the changed words within a line. It also compares whole folders, with filters for what to skip.

points.title: Beyond plain text
points.text: It compares images, with highlighted blocks and an overlay view, and shows CSV and TSV files as tables. With 7-Zip it can look inside archives, and plugins add more formats.

points.title: Ignore the noise
points.text: You can tell it to ignore whitespace, case or lines that match a regular expression, so only real changes show. It writes patches in normal, context or unified format and helps resolve conflict files.

points.title: Right-click from Explorer
points.text: Shell integration adds compare to Explorer's context menu, including on 64-bit Windows.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version. The project states support for Windows XP SP3 and newer, and the installers listed here cover x86, x64 and Arm64. The Windows listing keeps 33 versions.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: WinMerge is free under the GPL-2.0, with no paid edition.
